findings.description: All five issue forms say the operator applies `ready` once the ticket passes intake, which reverses ADR 0176: `ready` is applied first (by the operator or a write-access collaborator) and intake then checks the fields and removes it on failure.
findings.body:
**Who applies `ready`, and when, is backwards relative to decision 176.**

Each form's header says:

> Do not add the `ready` label yourself; the operator applies it once the ticket passes intake.

[ADR 0176](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/5f68aea03bdf48fba12547d046933d327d909e26/docs/adr/0176-a-ticket-has-a-type-and-only-some-types-need.md#L10-L12) says the opposite order:

> Only an issue carrying `ready`, applied by the operator or a collaborator with write access, is read. An intake agent checks the required fields before the label counts. On a failed check it comments which fields are missing or vague and removes the label.

So the label is what *triggers* intake. An operator or write-access collaborator who takes the form literally waits for intake to pass before labelling, and intake never starts. The form also drops the write-access collaborators the ADR allows. The rubrics under `docs/tickets/` already describe the ADR's order ("before the `ready` label counts"), so form and rubric now contradict each other.

Same sentence in all five forms: [bug.yml](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/5f68aea03bdf48fba12547d046933d327d909e26/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.yml#L10-L11), `chore-refactor.yml`, `docs-spike.yml`, `feature.yml`, `follow-up.yml` (lines 10-11). The suggestion fixes `bug.yml`. Make the same change in the other four, keeping each form's own rubric link.
findings.suggestion:
vague: [docs/tickets/bug.md](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/main/docs/tickets/bug.md). The operator or a
        collaborator with write access applies `ready`; intake then checks the fields and removes the label if any is missing or vague.

findings.description: Example commands and paths don't exist. The bug.yml placeholder `pup plan add t-1 --scope 'src/**'` passes a task id, but docs/02-cli.md:54 defines `pup plan add "<goal>"`. chore-refactor.yml (lines 32, 40-41) and docs/tickets/chore-refactor.md (lines 33-37) name `src/core/plan.service.ts`, `plan-store.service.ts` and `test/unit/core/plan-service.test.ts`, and none of those files exist. Use real commands and paths, or mark the examples as illustrative.

process_issues.description: Gated roster: spawned context (issue-form schema/ADR interplay), conventions, docs. Skipped correctness and security (no code logic and no trust boundary: only YAML issue forms and markdown), simplicity (the new files are the requested deliverable), guards (no non-test source), workflow-safety (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE, not .github/workflows), spec (no closing issue or --spec source), maintainability (off the default roster).
